pack.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
pack.publisher: OWASP GenAI Security Project (this pack is GovWren's own and is not published by OWASP)
pack.license: The source is published under CC BY-SA 4.0. This pack holds its risk codes with labels and summaries in GovWren's own words.
pack.attribution: The risk codes ASI01 to ASI10 of the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, each with a short label and a summary written for GovWren. Read the OWASP publication for the risks themselves and how to deal with them.

children.title: Goal hijack
children.text: Something the agent reads changes what it is trying to do.

children.title: Tool misuse
children.text: The agent uses a tool it was rightly given in a way nobody intended.

children.title: Identity and privilege abuse
children.text: The agent acts with access that belongs to someone else, or more access than its task needs.

children.title: Agentic supply chain
children.text: A tool, plug-in, prompt, or model the agent depends on is changed or was never what it seemed.

children.title: Unexpected code execution
children.text: The agent runs code or commands that reach beyond where they were meant to run.

children.title: Memory and context poisoning
children.text: What the agent remembers or looks up is altered so that later work goes wrong.

children.title: Insecure communication between agents
children.text: Agents accept messages from each other without knowing who sent them or whether they were changed.

children.title: Cascading failures
children.text: One agent's mistake spreads through the agents and systems that act on its output.

children.title: Exploiting people's trust in the agent
children.text: People accept what the agent says or asks for because it sounds sure, and act on it unchecked.

children.title: Rogue agents
children.text: An agent keeps acting outside what it was approved for, and nobody notices or can stop it.
